title: Taipei Zoo Plans a Walk to Keep Its Penguins Healthy
summaryZh: 北市動物園11/19讓非洲企鵝散步，預防圈養足部疾病。
summaryHi: ताइपे चिड़ियाघर 19 नवंबर को अफ़्रीकी पेंगुइनों को सैर कराएगा ताकि उनके पैर स्वस्थ रहें।
summaryEs: El zoo de Taipéi sacará a pasear a sus pingüinos africanos el 19 de noviembre para cuidar sus patas.
summaryJa: 台北市立動物園、11月19日にアフリカペンギンの散歩を実施、足の病気予防へ。
summaryKo: 타이베이 동물원, 11월 19일 아프리카펭귄 산책 행사… 발 질환 예방 목적.
summaryEn: Taipei Zoo will take its African penguins for a short supervised walk on 19 November to help prevent foot problems.
paragraphs: Taipei Zoo is preparing to let some of its African penguins stretch their legs. The zoo plans to hold a supervised 15-minute walk for the birds at 9:30 in the morning on Thursday, 19 November, provided the temperature stays below 24 degrees Celsius.

The event is intended to tackle a health risk. Penguins kept in captivity are prone to bumblefoot, a common foot condition that develops when a lack of exercise and excess weight place sustained pressure on their feet. Walking outside the enclosure gives the birds extra room to exercise and explore.

Keepers will lead the penguins along a designated section of the visitor pathway. However, the birds will be free to decide whether to leave their enclosure at all, and they can move at their own pace.

Visitors will be able to watch, but they must keep their voices down, stay behind the marked boundaries and avoid chasing, touching or feeding the animals. The zoo says the outing is mainly educational and that animal welfare comes first.

The African penguin is classified as critically endangered by the IUCN. Wild populations are shrinking rapidly due to competition with commercial fisheries, marine pollution and the degradation of their habitat.
Taipei Zoo has a fun plan. On 19 November, some African penguins will go for a walk outside their home.
The walk will start at 9:30 in the morning and last 15 minutes. It will only happen if the weather is cool, under 24 degrees.
Why a walk? Penguins in zoos can get bad feet. This happens when they do not move much and get too heavy. Walking helps them stay healthy.
Zoo workers will lead the birds along a path for visitors. The penguins can choose to come out or stay in. People can watch them, but they must be quiet. They must not touch, chase or feed the birds.
African penguins are in great danger in the wild. Their numbers are falling fast.
sentZh: 台北市立動物園有一個有趣的計畫。
11月19日，一些非洲企鵝將到牠們的家外面散步。
散步將在早上9點30分開始，持續15分鐘。
只有在天氣涼爽、低於24度時才會舉行。
為什麼要散步？
動物園裡的企鵝腳可能會出問題。
這種情況發生在牠們不常活動、變得太重的時候。
散步能幫助牠們保持健康。
動物園人員會帶領企鵝沿著遊客步道走。
企鵝可以選擇出來或留在裡面。
民眾可以觀看，但必須保持安靜。
他們不可以觸摸、追逐或餵食企鵝。
非洲企鵝在野外面臨很大的危險。
牠們的數量正快速減少。

paragraphs: Taipei Zoo is planning a special event for some of its smallest residents. On Thursday, 19 November, a group of African penguins will leave their enclosure for a 15-minute walk, starting at 9:30 in the morning.
The walk will only go ahead if the temperature is below 24 degrees Celsius. The zoo calls it its first "Penguin Outing Day" this year.

According to the zoo, penguins that live in captivity can develop a common foot problem called bumblefoot. It happens when the birds do not get enough exercise and become overweight, which puts constant pressure on their feet. A walk gives them more space to move and explore.

Keepers will guide the penguins along part of the visitor path, but the birds can decide for themselves whether to come out. Visitors are asked to keep their voices down and not to chase, touch or feed the penguins.
The African penguin is listed as critically endangered. In the wild, its numbers are falling quickly because of pollution, the loss of its habitat and competition with fishing boats for food.
sentZh: 台北市立動物園正在為一些最小的住民規劃一場特別活動。
11月19日星期四，一群非洲企鵝將離開牠們的展區，進行15分鐘的散步，從早上9點30分開始。
只有在氣溫低於攝氏24度時，散步才會舉行。
動物園稱這是今年第一次的「企鵝出遊日」。
根據動物園的說法，圈養的企鵝可能會罹患一種常見的足部問題，叫做趾瘤症。
當企鵝運動不足、體重過重時就會發生，這會讓牠們的腳持續承受壓力。
散步能給牠們更多空間活動和探索。
保育員會引導企鵝沿著部分遊客步道行走，但企鵝可以自己決定是否出來。
遊客被要求降低音量，不要追逐、觸摸或餵食企鵝。
非洲企鵝被列為極度瀕危物種。
在野外，由於污染、棲息地喪失以及與漁船爭奪食物，牠們的數量正迅速減少。

sentZh: 台北市立動物園準備讓部分非洲企鵝出來伸展雙腿。

這項活動旨在應對一項健康風險。

到展區外散步能給企鵝額外的空間運動和探索。
保育員會帶領企鵝沿著遊客步道的指定路段行走。
不過，企鵝可以自由決定是否要離開展區，也能按照自己的步調移動。

paragraphs: Visitors to Taipei Zoo next week may witness an unusual sight: a line of African penguins waddling along a public walkway. The zoo has scheduled a supervised, 15-minute outing for the birds at 9:30 in the morning on 19 November, although the event will proceed only if temperatures remain below 24 degrees Celsius.

Behind the charming spectacle lies a serious purpose. Captive penguins are susceptible to bumblefoot, a common foot condition caused by prolonged pressure on the soles, which in turn stems from insufficient exercise and excess weight. By giving the birds a larger area to roam, keepers hope to keep them active and healthy.
Crucially, participation is voluntary. Keepers will guide the penguins along a designated stretch of the visitor path, but each bird may choose whether to venture out and can set its own pace.

Spectators have been asked to keep noise to a minimum and to refrain from chasing, touching or feeding the penguins. Describing the event, the zoo stressed that its primary aim is education and that animal welfare takes priority.

The outing also highlights the plight of the species, which the IUCN lists as critically endangered. In the wild, African penguin numbers are falling sharply as a result of competition with commercial fishing, marine pollution, habitat degradation and human disturbance.
sentZh: 下週到台北市立動物園的遊客可能會看到不尋常的景象：一排非洲企鵝搖搖擺擺地走在公共步道上。
動物園已安排在11月19日早上9點30分為企鵝舉辦一場有人監督的15分鐘出遊，不過只有在氣溫維持在攝氏24度以下時才會進行。
在這個可愛景象的背後，有著嚴肅的目的。
圈養企鵝容易罹患趾瘤症，這是一種常見的足部疾病，起因是腳底長時間受壓，而這又源於運動不足和體重過重。
保育員希望藉由給企鵝更大的活動範圍，讓牠們保持活躍和健康。
關鍵在於，參加完全出於自願。
保育員會引導企鵝沿著遊客步道的指定路段行走，但每隻企鵝都可以選擇是否要冒險出來，並自行決定步調。
觀眾被要求盡量降低噪音，並避免追逐、觸摸或餵食企鵝。
動物園在介紹這項活動時強調，其主要目的是教育，而且動物福祉優先。
這次出遊也凸顯了這個物種的困境，IUCN已將其列為極度瀕危。
在野外，由於與商業捕魚競爭、海洋污染、棲息地退化和人類干擾，非洲企鵝的數量正急遽下降。

paragraphs: Taipei Zoo has announced plans to take a group of African penguins on a supervised walk outside their enclosure. The 15-minute excursion is scheduled for 9:30 in the morning on 19 November, but it will take place only if the temperature is below 24 degrees Celsius.

According to the zoo, the initiative addresses a significant welfare concern. Penguins in captivity are vulnerable to bumblefoot, a common condition that arises when inadequate exercise and excessive weight subject their feet to constant pressure. Providing additional space in which to exercise and explore is therefore regarded as beneficial.

Notably, the birds will not be compelled to take part. Although keepers will escort them along a designated section of the visitor pathway, each penguin may decide whether to leave the enclosure and may proceed at its own pace.

Members of the public will be permitted to observe, provided that they lower their voices, remain behind designated boundaries and refrain from chasing, touching or feeding the animals. The zoo has emphasised that the event is primarily educational and that animal welfare remains its foremost priority.

The initiative also draws attention to the precarious status of the species, which is classified as critically endangered by the IUCN. Wild populations are declining rapidly owing to competition with commercial fisheries, marine pollution, habitat degradation and human disturbance.
sentZh: 台北市立動物園宣布計畫帶一群非洲企鵝到展區外進行有人監督的散步。
這趟15分鐘的出遊預定於11月19日早上9點30分舉行，但只有在氣溫低於攝氏24度時才會進行。
據動物園表示，這項計畫是為了處理一項重大的動物福祉問題。
圈養的企鵝容易罹患趾瘤症，這是一種常見疾病，當運動不足和體重過重使牠們的腳持續承受壓力時就會出現。
因此，提供額外的空間讓牠們運動和探索被認為是有益的。
值得注意的是，企鵝不會被強迫參加。
雖然保育員會護送牠們沿著遊客步道的指定路段行走，但每隻企鵝都可以決定是否離開展區，並能按照自己的步調前進。
民眾可以觀看，前提是要降低音量、待在指定界線後方，並避免追逐、觸摸或餵食動物。
動物園強調，這項活動主要是為了教育，而動物福祉仍是其首要考量。
這項計畫也讓人關注到這個物種岌岌可危的處境，牠已被IUCN列為極度瀕危。
由於與商業漁業競爭、海洋污染、棲息地退化和人類干擾，野生族群正迅速減少。

keepers.en: people who look after animals in a zoo
keepers.ex: The keepers feed the penguins fish.

kept.ex: Animals kept in zoos need exercise.

lack.en: the state of not having enough
lack.ex: The project failed because of a lack of money.

last.en: coming at the end (at the last minute: very late)
last.ex: He packed his bag at the last minute.

lead.ex: She will lead the team next season.

leave.en: to go away from a place

legs.en: the body parts used for walking
legs.ex: Stretch your legs after a long trip.

lies.ex: The answer lies in better training.

line.en: a row of people or things
line.ex: A line of ducks crossed the road.

listed.en: officially named in a list or category
listed.ex: The building is listed as historic.

lists.en: officially names in a list or category
lists.ex: The group lists the frog as endangered.

live.en: to spend your life in a place

loss.ex: The loss of forests harms wildlife.

lower.en: to make something less loud or high

mainly.ex: The class is mainly for beginners.

marked.ex: Park only in the marked spaces.

members.en: people who belong to a group
members.ex: Members of the public may visit.

morning.en: the early part of the day

notably.ex: Notably, sales rose during the winter.

november.en: the eleventh month of the year

observe.ex: Visitors can observe seals from the cliff.

on.en: used with days and dates; about

out.en: away from inside a place (roll out: introduce)

outing.ex: The school planned an outing to the zoo.

pace.en: the speed at which someone moves

part.ex: Teachers will take part in the strike.

path.en: a narrow way for walking or cycling
path.ex: A narrow path leads down to the beach.

pathway.en: a path for people to walk along
pathway.ex: Follow the pathway to the lake.

penguin.en: a black and white sea bird that cannot fly
penguin.ex: The penguin dived into the cold water.

penguins.en: black and white sea birds that cannot fly
penguins.ex: The penguins swam around the pool.

permitted.ex: Dogs are not permitted on the beach.

place.en: to put something (e.g. pressure) on someone or something
place.ex: Extra weight can place stress on joints.

planning.ex: They are planning a trip to Japan.

plans.ex: The town has plans for a new park.

plight.ex: The film shows the plight of wild tigers.

note.usage: 常見 the plight of + 人/動物；highlight the plight。

example.en: The documentary shows the plight of farmers in the drought.
example.zh: 這部紀錄片呈現了乾旱中農民的困境。

noteHi.usage: the plight of + लोग/जानवर आम प्रयोग है।
noteHi.exampleTr: यह वृत्तचित्र सूखे में किसानों की दुर्दशा दिखाता है।

noteEs.usage: Se usa the plight of + personas/animales.
noteEs.exampleTr: El documental muestra la difícil situación de los agricultores en la sequía.

noteJa.usage: the plight of + 人／動物 の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: そのドキュメンタリーは干ばつに苦しむ農家の窮状を描く。

noteKo.usage: the plight of + 사람/동물 형태가 흔하다.
noteKo.exampleTr: 그 다큐멘터리는 가뭄 속 농민들의 곤경을 보여 준다.

pollution.en: dirty or harmful things in air, water or land
pollution.ex: Cars cause a lot of pollution.

populations.en: groups of a species living in an area
populations.ex: Bird populations fell in the dry years.

precarious.ex: Many families face a precarious situation.

example.en: The club is in a precarious financial position.
example.zh: 該俱樂部的財務狀況岌岌可危。

note.usage: precarious situation/position/finances；強調隨時可能惡化。

noteHi.exampleTr: क्लब की आर्थिक स्थिति अनिश्चित है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El club está en una situación financiera precaria.

noteJa.exampleTr: そのクラブは財政的に不安定な状況にある。

noteEn.meaning: not safe; likely to get worse.

preparing.ex: Workers are preparing for the strike.

pressure.en: strong demand or force from people
pressure.ex: There is pressure on the company to cut prices.

primarily.ex: The course is primarily for adults.

priority.zh: 優先事項（top priority：首要任務）

problem.ex: There was a problem with the bus.

proceed.ex: The meeting will proceed as planned.

prone.ex: Tired drivers are prone to mistakes.

provided.ex: You can go, provided you finish early.

providing.ex: The charity is providing food for families.

public.ex: The park is open to the public.

purpose.ex: The purpose of the meeting is clear.

puts.en: causes something (e.g. pressure) to affect something
puts.ex: Too much weight puts stress on the knees.

quiet.ex: Please be quiet in the library.

example.en: Please refrain from using phones during the show.
example.zh: 演出期間請勿使用手機。

note.usage: refrain from + 名詞/V-ing，常見於告示與正式建議。

noteHi.exampleTr: शो के दौरान कृपया फ़ोन का उपयोग न करें।

noteEs.exampleTr: Por favor, absténganse de usar el móvil durante la función.

noteJa.exampleTr: 上演中は携帯電話の使用をお控えください。
noteJa.usage: refrain from + 名詞/-ing、掲示や正式な助言で。

noteKo.exampleTr: 공연 중 휴대전화 사용을 삼가 주세요.

noteEn.meaning: to stop yourself from doing something.

regarded.en: thought of in a particular way
regarded.ex: He is regarded as the best player on the team.

remain.ex: Most visitors remain in the city centre.

remains.ex: Most visitors remain in the city centre.

residents.en: people who live in a place

result.zh: 結果（as a result of：由於）
result.ja: 結果（as a result of：〜の結果）
result.en: in "as a result of": because of
result.ex: Prices rose as a result of the storm.

risk.en: the chance that something bad will happen
risk.ex: Smoking increases the risk of disease.

roam.en: to move around without a fixed plan
roam.ex: Goats roam freely on the hill.

room.en: space for moving or doing something
room.ex: The animals need more room to run.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

scheduled.ex: The meeting is scheduled for Monday.

section.ex: This section of the highway is closed today.

set.ex: Each runner can set their own speed.

sight.ex: The sunset was a beautiful sight.

significant.ex: There was a significant rise in rents.

smallest.ex: This is the smallest room in the house.

soles.en: the bottom surfaces of the feet
soles.ex: Hot sand burned the soles of my feet.

space.en: a room or area used for something
space.ex: The library is a quiet space for study.

special.ex: The area has a special feeling.

species.en: a group of similar animals or plants

spectacle.en: an unusual or impressive thing to watch
spectacle.ex: The parade was a colourful spectacle.

starting.en: beginning at a place or time
starting.ex: Starting at the station, the walk takes an hour.

status.en: the situation of someone at a given time
status.ex: Please check the status of your order.

stay.ex: Most tourists stay in the centre.

stays.ex: The road stays open all night.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

stretch.en: to extend your body; a section of a path
stretch.ex: This stretch of road is busy.

subject.en: to make someone or something experience something unpleasant
subject.ex: Heavy loads subject the bridge to strain.

supervised.en: watched over by a responsible person
supervised.ex: Children may swim only in supervised areas.

susceptible.en: likely to be harmed by something
susceptible.ex: Old people are susceptible to colds.

note.meaning: 容易受影響的；易感染的。
note.usage: 常見 susceptible to + 疾病/損害。

example.en: Older trees are more susceptible to storm damage.
example.zh: 老樹更容易受到暴風雨破壞。

noteHi.usage: susceptible to + रोग/नुकसान आम प्रयोग है।
noteHi.exampleTr: पुराने पेड़ तूफ़ान से जल्दी नुकसान उठाते हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los árboles viejos son más propensos a los daños por tormentas.

noteJa.meaning: 影響を受けやすい；かかりやすい。
noteJa.usage: susceptible to + 病気／被害 の形が多い。
noteJa.exampleTr: 古い木は嵐の被害を受けやすい。

noteKo.exampleTr: 오래된 나무는 폭풍 피해를 입기 쉽다.

noteEn.meaning: easily affected or harmed by something.

sustained.ex: The city saw a sustained rise in tourism.

tackle.ex: The city must tackle air pollution.

take.zh: 參加；發生（take part / take place）
take.ex: The meeting will take place on Friday.

takes.en: in "takes priority": is treated as most important

temperature.en: how hot or cold something is

temperatures.ex: Temperatures dropped below zero last night.

themselves.en: without anyone doing it; on their own

therefore.ex: It was late; therefore, we took a taxi.

touch.en: to put your hand on something

touching.ex: Touching the paintings is not allowed.

turn.en: in "in turn": as a result of that
turn.ex: Rain caused floods, which in turn closed roads.

unusual.ex: It is unusual for the bank to speak during trading.

venture.en: to go somewhere that may be new or a little risky
venture.ex: Few people venture out in the storm.

visitor.en: a person who goes to see a place
visitor.ex: The visitor path runs past the pool.

voices.en: the sounds people make when they speak
voices.ex: Please lower your voices in the library.

voluntary.en: done by choice, not by law
voluntary.ex: Joining the club is completely voluntary.

vulnerable.ex: Old computers are vulnerable to viruses.
vulnerable.ja: 脆弱な；攻撃されやすい

example.en: Children are especially vulnerable to the cold.
example.zh: 兒童特別容易受到寒冷的影響。

note.meaning: 容易受到攻擊、傷害或影響的；脆弱的。
note.usage: 常用 be vulnerable to + 名詞，表示容易受某事物傷害；可形容人、系統或地區。

noteHi.exampleTr: बच्चे ठंड के प्रति विशेष रूप से संवेदनशील होते हैं।
noteHi.meaning: जिस पर आसानी से हमला हो सके या जिसे नुकसान पहुँच सके; कमज़ोर।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर be vulnerable to + संज्ञा के रूप में प्रयोग होता है।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los niños son especialmente vulnerables al frío.
noteEs.meaning: fácil de atacar o dañar; frágil.
noteEs.usage: Se usa a menudo como be vulnerable to + sustantivo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 子どもは特に寒さに弱い。
noteJa.meaning: 攻撃や被害を受けやすい；脆弱な。
noteJa.usage: be vulnerable to + 名詞「〜に弱い・さらされやすい」の形でよく使う。

noteKo.usage: 주로 be vulnerable to + 명사(~에 취약하다) 형태로 쓴다.

noteEn.usage: Often used as 'vulnerable to' something; can describe people, systems or places.

waddling.en: walking with short steps, moving from side to side
waddling.ex: Ducks were waddling across the road.

walk.en: a journey on foot, often for pleasure
walk.ex: We went for a walk in the park.

walking.en: the activity of going on foot
walking.ex: Walking is good for your health.

walkway.en: a path for people to walk on
walkway.ex: A covered walkway joins the buildings.

weather.ex: The weather in Ireland changes quickly.

weight.en: how heavy a person or animal is

welfare.en: help and care for people's health and comfort
welfare.ex: The charity works for child welfare.

whether.en: used to express a choice (if or not)

wild.en: living in nature, not on farms

witness.ex: Visitors may witness a rare event.

workers.ex: Public sector workers want higher pay.

zoo.en: a place where wild animals are kept for people to see
zoo.ex: We saw pandas at the zoo.

zoos.en: places where wild animals are kept for people to see
zoos.ex: Many zoos help protect rare animals.
